High-pressure optical floating-zone growth under 20 bar oxygen pressure was used to successfully grow single crystals of La4Ni3O10.
The as-grown crystal (S1) had the Bmab structure, while the annealed crystal (S2) had the P2_1/a structure.
The metal-to-metal transitions occurred at 152 K for the Bmab structured crystal (S1) and 136 K for the P2_1/a structured crystal (S2).
The magnetic susceptibility data showed sharp anomalies at the metal-to-metal transition temperatures, indicating high sample quality.
The analysis of the magnetization data suggested the presence of only about 0.4 ‰/f.u. of quasi-free spins with S=1.
The entropy changes associated with the metal-to-metal transition were around 1.4-1.6 J/(mol·K) for both the P2_1/a and Bmab structured crystals.
Magnetic field had only insignificant effects on the metal-to-metal transition temperature, as confirmed by specific heat measurements at 14 T.
The specific heat anomalies in the authors' crystals were much sharper compared to previously reported anomalies, likely indicating excellent crystallinity.
The shape of the specific heat anomaly for the Bmab structured crystal suggested a discontinuous character of the metal-to-metal transition.
The authors were able to avoid the formation of a previously reported ferromagnetic impurity phase by using the growth conditions reported in this study.
The post-annealing process under high oxygen pressure led to a notable reduction of the impurity phase in the crystals.
The authors used powder X-ray diffraction and Laue diffraction to characterize the phase purity and crystallinity of the grown single crystals.
The feed and seed rod velocities were optimized at 6 mm/h and 4 mm/h, respectively, to maintain a stable melting zone during the growth.
The temperature of the melting zone during growth was determined to be around 1650°C using an in-situ two-color pyrometer.
The authors performed rapid cooling of the as-grown boule as well as further high-pressure annealing to obtain the different crystal structures.
